title: Molina: consent to prevenient grace is wholly supernatural, yet free (Concordia, disp. 40)
source_text: XII. Quae doctrina est ipsius Ludovici Molinae. Docet enim consensum quem voluntas nostra praebet Deo per gratiam praevenientem vocanti, a Deo esse non tantum tanquam ab alliciente, invitante, & excitante, sed etiam tanquam a cooperante per auxilium gratiae; adeoque in eo consensu nihil reipsa esse quod supernaturale non sit; ac proinde adultum nihil habere, in iis quae ad justificationem necessaria sunt, de quo gloriari possit, & quod a Deo per gratiam non acceperit. Sic enim ex antepositis quibusdam ratiocinatur. Quo fit ut consensus liberi arbitrii Deo excitanti ac vocanti per gratiam praevenientem, nihil in re sit quod non sit supernaturale, & quod non simul a Deo emanet, non solum tanquam ab alliciente, excitante, & invitante ad id arbitrium nostrum, sed etiam tanquam a cooperante per auxilium gratiae, atque adeo fit ut nihil omnino habeat adultus ex iis, quae ad justificationem sunt necessaria, & quibus a non justificato discernatur, de quo gloriari possit, ac si id a Deo non acceperit; tametsi ad multa ex iis, quae ad justificationem sunt necessaria, libere cooperetur ac influat; ita ut in ipsius potestate sit non cooperari, & non influere, atque adeo impedire ne in rerum natura existant. Disputatione 40. ad art. 3. quaest. 14.
pass_a_gloss: XII. Which doctrine is that of Luis de Molina himself. For he teaches that the consent which our will gives to God calling through prevenient grace, is from God not only as from one alluring, inviting, and arousing, but also as from one cooperating through the help of grace; and so in that consent there is nothing in reality which is not supernatural; and accordingly that the adult has nothing, in those things which are necessary for justification, of which he can glory, and which he has not received from God through grace. For thus he reasons from certain things set down before. Whence it comes that in the consent of free choice to God arousing and calling through prevenient grace, there is nothing in reality which is not supernatural, and which does not at the same time emanate from God, not only as from one alluring, arousing, and inviting our choice to it, but also as from one cooperating through the help of grace, and so it comes that the adult has nothing at all of those things which are necessary for justification, and by which he is distinguished from one not justified, of which he can glory, as if he had not received it from God; although to many of those things which are necessary for justification he freely cooperates and contributes; so that it is in his power not to cooperate, and not to contribute, and so to hinder them from existing in the nature of things. Disputation 40, on article 3 of question 14.
pass_b_english: This is the teaching of Luis de Molina himself. He holds that the consent our will gives to God calling it through prevenient grace comes from God not only as one who attracts, invites and rouses, but also as one who cooperates through the help of grace. So there is nothing in that consent that is not in fact supernatural, and in what is needed for justification the adult has nothing to boast of that he has not received from God through grace.

He reasons this way from earlier premises: 'Hence in the consent of free choice to God, who rouses and calls through prevenient grace, there is in fact nothing that is not supernatural and does not also come from God, not only as attracting, rousing and inviting our choice to it, but also as cooperating through the help of grace.

So the adult has nothing at all, among the things needed for justification and by which he is set apart from the unjustified, that he can boast of as though he had not received it from God; even though in many of the things needed for justification he freely cooperates and contributes, so that it is in his power not to cooperate or contribute, and so to prevent them from coming into existence.' Disputation 40, on article 3 of question 14.
